title: AI on arXiv — daily notable papers, 23 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from sparse attention signals and cross-list breadth, with limited citation evidence for recent papers. This is not a measure of readership or overall importance.

sections.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
sections.abstract: The authors present a frozen audio-forgery detector evaluated across ten public benchmarks, multiple generators, recording conditions and languages, reporting strong results including first place on Podonos and the lowest commercial-detector equal error rate on ASVspoof5.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a single frozen model generalizes across audio generators, channels, recording settings, and languages, with the benchmark and leaderboard results summarized in the arXiv abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports benchmark and leaderboard evaluations but does not describe prospective deployment or error rates across operational populations; the claimed generality should be read within the tested settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Highest signal score in the pool (1.636): Semantic Scholar reports 1 current citation (weighted component 1.386), plus 1 cross-list (0.25). No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: Towards Text-Mask Consistency in Medical Image Segmentation
sections.abstract: The authors introduce C2Seg, combining cluster-aware soft contrastive labels, bidirectional complementary attention, and KAN-based attention gating to improve text-mask consistency and segmentation accuracy on four public medical-imaging datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors attribute improved text-mask consistency and segmentation accuracy to C2Seg and report results on four public datasets (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence in the abstract is limited to four public datasets; it does not establish performance across other clinical sites or deployment workflows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.386, entirely from 1 current Semantic Scholar citation (weighted component 1.386); no cross-list contribution. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components. The arXiv record notes ICLR 2026 poster acceptance.

sections.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
sections.abstract: The authors model agent states and a global potential to describe how post-training organizes LLM-agent reasoning, demonstrating the framework on safety-test selection and physics-reasoning audits using Qwen3.5-9B.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose agent states as measurable intermediate variables and report that potential structure strengthens during post-training in their two Qwen3.5-9B tasks (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The empirical demonstration described in the abstract uses one model family and two tasks, so it does not establish that the proposed state/potential account transfers broadly.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.000, entirely from 4 cross-listings (weighted component 1.000), including cs.AI and cs.CL; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
sections.abstract: The authors replace free-form LLM generation with predefined-answer classification for translating natural-language instructions into linear temporal logic, reporting comparable or better accuracy than local LLMs on three benchmarks at up to an order of magnitude lower runtime and energy use.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a System-One classifier approach matches or exceeds the best local LLMs on three benchmarks and generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not specify how the benchmark results translate to safety or reliability in physical deployments; the reported evidence is benchmark-based.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.000 from 4 cross-listings (weighted component 1.000), including AI, language, and robotics; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
sections.abstract: SecretAgent uses LLM agents to identify image evidence that reveals private information and iteratively tune low-visibility perturbations; the authors report privacy and image-fidelity results across four applications, five datasets, and six VLMs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim the framework improves image fidelity while achieving state-of-the-art privacy protection in the four tested applications and transfers to other VLMs (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract evaluations cover five datasets and six VLMs; privacy against other model families, image transformations, or attacker capabilities is not established there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.000 from 4 cross-listings (weighted component 1.000), including AI, machine learning, and multiagent systems; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
sections.abstract: Baton maps a small VLM visual KV cache into a larger VLM memory for uncertain decisions; the authors report near re-watching performance with 28–47% less compute and up to 8× less compute per escalation at 64 frames.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a learned per-layer linear map lets the larger model reuse the smaller model visual memory, with results on RoboMME and zero-shot transfer to OpenEQA (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The reported compute and performance results are tied to the evaluated model pairs, datasets, and escalation setup; broader deployment costs are not established in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.000 from 4 cross-listings (weighted component 1.000), spanning AI, language, learning, and robotics; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
sections.abstract: SLP-Bench scores acoustic claims in audio-language-model reasoning against clinician ratings across five datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions; the authors report that zero-shot claims are imperfect and unstable, while GRPO fine-tuning improves claim accuracy and agreement.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute a clinician-referenced benchmark for checking factuality, stability, and consistency of acoustic reasoning claims, and report a GRPO fine-tuning improvement (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: Dataset access is available on request and subject to the providers approval, which may constrain independent reproduction (arXiv abstract).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.750 from 3 cross-listings (weighted component 0.750), including AI, language, and learning; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: Embodied-Harness pairs an acting agent with a reflector that turns execution evidence into reusable guidance without updating model parameters; the authors report results on three benchmarks and real-world trials across three manipulation tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench, plus 96.7% average success across three real-world tasks (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes real-world evaluation on only three manipulation tasks; broader task and environment coverage remains unshown there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.750 from 3 cross-listings (weighted component 0.750), connecting robotics, AI, vision, and multiagent systems; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: PLoQ: A Prompt-Specific Low-Rank Basis for 4-bit Quantization of LLM Activations
sections.abstract: PLoQ estimates a prompt-specific low-rank basis during prefill, quantizes dominant activation directions separately, and restores them within the matrix multiplication; the authors report improvements over mixed-precision baselines on six Llama and Qwen models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report better perplexity recovery than the compared quantization method across six models from 1B to 70B parameters, with modest reported prefill and decode overhead on Llama-3.1-8B (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison uses a particular mixed-precision setup and sequence lengths up to 8k tokens (16k for two models); results beyond those configurations are not established in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.750 from 3 cross-listings (weighted component 0.750), spanning learning, language, and computer systems; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations. No HF/HN points surfaced in the candidate score components.

sections.title: Contexture: Runtime Context Eviction for High-Throughput Agent Serving
sections.abstract: Contexture uses tool-operation history and runtime cache state to evict superseded context from agent execution while preserving the full conversation record; the authors report higher throughput under service-level objectives across two models, two harnesses, and two benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 20–73% throughput improvement over the best listed baselines under SLO in tested configurations and up to 11% lower GPU energy per completed session (arXiv abstract).
sections.unique_caveat: Live-agent experiments report a worst-case accuracy loss of 3.7 percentage points versus unloaded no-eviction, despite a 1.4-point mean gain; throughput benefits therefore need to be considered alongside accuracy (arXiv abstract).
